bibliographic_identity.title: Rebonds: Structural Affordances, Negotiation, and Creation

production_source_extensions.registration_reason: Comparative recording analysis of ten Rebonds interpretations used as methodological support for performance-led analysis. It explicitly distinguishes tempo and pitch measurements from by-ear study of accent articulation and grouping structure and argues that recordings can disclose structural affordances unavailable to score-only analysis.

locators.section: Status and purpose of the article's videos
locators.supports: The authors state that the videos presented in the article were recorded by the article authors and are exclusively illustrative, intended to animate theoretical discussion of difficult excerpts. They also state that the reported study processes and performance solutions are not intended as normative prescriptions.

locators.pages: Rebonds B, §2.1, Figure 3 / footnote 8 and Figure 4 / footnote 10
locators.supports: The article links the same illustrative video, YouTube ID OsEU0xr6bSs, at 0:31 for the Figure 3 drag solution and at 1:00 for the authors' proposed Figure 4 sticking solution.

For the increasingly complex drag passage around mm. 61–64, the article links OsEU0xr6bSs at 1:29 and states that the excerpt first demonstrates the Figure 2 sticking slowly and quickly, then the Figure 3 sticking slowly and quickly.

source_reviews.rights_and_reuse_note: The publisher article is available for scholarly review and its bibliographic and locator data are stored only as metadata/paraphrase. The article identifies the linked video as author-recorded and illustrative, but no license for the YouTube media itself is assumed from the article license; no audiovisual bytes are copied or embedded.

locators.supports: Duinker analyzes audio from ten commercially recorded interpretations of Rebonds across tempo, pitch, accent articulation, grouping structure and selected score-fidelity questions; tempo and pitch are treated computationally, while accent and grouping are studied by ear.

The study frames performances as evidence that can reveal or generate structural aspects that score-centered analysis cannot easily illuminate and uses recordings as an entry point for a pluralistic, performance-sensitive conception of structure.

source_reviews.rights_and_reuse_note: History Go stores only bibliographic identity, DOI, section locators and paraphrased methodological findings from the publisher-hosted article; article text, figures and referenced recordings are not redistributed.

release_candidate.proposed_scope: A timecoded, descriptive comparison of the audible difference between the concrete Rebonds B performance solutions demonstrated in the author-recorded illustrative object, especially the paired slow/fast comparison at 1:29 for mm. 61–64.
explicit_nonclaims: No claim that one execution is the uniquely correct performance.
No claim that the article authors' evaluative language is itself a direct sonic observation by History Go.

resolved: Labrada, Chaib & Braga Leandro full text reviewed; the authors identify the videos as author-recorded illustrative material and the Rebonds B video ID is fixed as OsEU0xr6bSs.
Three article-provided object locators are fixed at 0:31, 1:00 and 1:29, with 1:29 explicitly tied to the mm. 61–64 slow/fast comparison of two sticking solutions.
Duinker's comparative recording-analysis methodology is fulltext-reviewed, and media rights are conservatively limited to external_link_and_metadata_only.
unresolved: The recording/performance date of the YouTube object has not been independently verified.
